issues.title: Internal class missing sealed keyword
issues.description: Internal implementation classes that are not designed for inheritance must be marked with the 'sealed' keyword. The WebSocketWrapper class is an internal implementation class that should be sealed to prevent unintended subclassing.
issues.rule_name: Sealed Keyword Required for Internal Implementation Classes

issues.title: Incorrect boolean operator in regex validation
issues.description: The test assertion uses AND (&&) operator instead of OR (||) when checking if the log message matches either the old or new CSP error pattern. This causes the test to fail because a log message cannot simultaneously match both regex patterns - they represent different browser error message formats. The original intent was to accept either format, but the AND operator requires both patterns to match at the same time, which is impossible. This will cause the test to fail even when receiving a valid CSP error message in either format.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
Assert.True(
    ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(logs[0].Message) &&
    ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(logs[0].Message),
    $"Expected log message to match one of the CSP error patterns: {ParseErrorMessageRegexOld} or {ParseErrorMessageRegexNew}. Actual: {logs[0].Message}");

issues.title: Disposal order causing potential race condition
issues.description: The connection disposal order is reversed - disposing secondConnection before the connection that is still being used. In the test, 'connection' performs an InvokeAsync call and its TaskCompletionSource (tcs) is awaited immediately before disposal. However, disposing secondConnection first may cause premature cleanup of shared resources or message handlers since both connections share the same user ('*'). This can lead to flaky test behavior where the connection's pending operations are interrupted by the disposal of secondConnection, especially in distributed scenarios where both connections interact with the same Redis backplane.

issues.title: Race condition from premature TaskCompletionSource recreation
issues.description: The _receiveTcs TaskCompletionSource is recreated before checking if the buffer is zero-sized, creating a race condition in the WebSocketWrapper's ReceiveAsync implementation. When a zero-byte read occurs (buffer.Count == 0), the method returns early with the result but the TCS has already been reset. This means if another thread or the background task tries to set a result on the now-recreated TCS while this zero-byte read is in progress, it will affect the next receive operation rather than completing the current one. This breaks the synchronization contract and can cause message loss or out-of-order receives in the stateful reconnection test scenarios where WebSocket message sequencing is critical.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The modified test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate phases, violating the required AAA comment pattern.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64685 - [release/9.0] Update dependencies from dotnet/arcade

structured_output.summary:
This is a Maestro-driven Arcade bump on release/9.0, moving from 9.0.0-beta.25562.4 to 9.0.0-beta.25626.6. Most of it is routine. Version.Details.xml, Versions.props and global.json are updated. The vendored `eng/common` scripts pick up `-UseBasicParsing`, tolerate a missing `tools.vs` in `LocateVisualStudio`, and point at the `ci.dot.net` feed and the azurelinux-3 image. The source-index template now defaults to running on main only. All of that is consistent with upstream Arcade.

The PR also changes two test files, and both changes have real bugs. In `WebSocketCompressionTests`, the new check meant to accept either the old or the new Chrome CSP message joins the two regexes with `&&`. One message can't match both, so the assertion always fails. In `RedisEndToEnd.WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync`, the line that replaces the TaskCompletionSource now runs before the zero-byte-read early return. The SignalR client always issues a zero-byte read before the real read, so that read now consumes each message and throws its payload away. The other test changes look fine: two new `[QuarantinedTest]` attributes, the swapped dispose order, and dropping `sealed`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The dependency and `eng/common` updates are fine. The CSP assertion, though, can never pass, and the wrapper's zero-byte-read change drops every received message in the stateful-reconnect test. Both should be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Arcade dependency flow works like this: Maestro opens a PR that bumps the versions in `eng/Version.Details.xml`, `eng/Versions.props` and the `global.json` msbuild-sdks entries, and syncs the shared `eng/common` scripts and pipeline templates from the matching Arcade commit. Those scripts (`tools.ps1`, the core-templates) run the CI bootstrap: installing dotnet, finding VS/MSBuild, and running the source-build and source-index jobs.

On top of the infra sync, this PR changes two test files. A Blazor E2E test (`BlockedWebSocketCompressionTests`) is rewritten to accept either of two Chrome CSP log formats. A Redis backplane test helper (`WebSocketWrapper`) changes when it resets its receive TaskCompletionSource. That helper sits between the SignalR client's `WebSocketsTransport` receive loop and a background pump that reads from the real `ClientWebSocket`.
steps: Start with `eng/Version.Details.xml`, `eng/Versions.props` and `global.json`. These are the mechanical version and SHA bumps to 9.0.0-beta.25626.6.

Next, the `eng/common` sync. `tools.ps1` (`-UseBasicParsing`, null-safe `vs` lookup in `LocateVisualStudio`), `internal-feed-operations.ps1` and `nuget-verification.ps1` all come straight from upstream Arcade.

Then the pipeline templates: the source-build pool image moves to `1es-azurelinux-3`, the internal runtime feed moves to `ci.dot.net`, and source-index defaults to main only (ci.yml already gates it to main).
In `WebSocketCompressionTests.cs`, the single `Assert.Matches` is replaced by two partial-property `GeneratedRegex` patterns combined into one boolean check.

In `RedisEndToEnd.cs`, the `_receiveTcs` reset in `WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync` moves above the zero-byte-read check. That changes how the wrapper hands off data to the `WebSocketsTransport` zero-byte-then-real read pattern.

findings.title: CSP log assertion uses && so it can never pass
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/WebSocketCompressionTests.cs`, lines 107-110, `EmbeddingServerAppInsideIframe_WithCompressionEnabled_Fails` combines `ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(...)` and `ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(...)` with `&&`. The two patterns are mutually exclusive (old vs. new Chrome CSP wording), so the assertion always fails. Change `&&` to `||` so the test accepts either format, as the assertion message already says. Keep the descriptive failure message.

findings.title: WebSocketWrapper zero-byte read now consumes and drops each message
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs`, `WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync` (around lines 406-417) now resets `_receiveTcs` before the `buffer.Count == 0` early return. `WebSocketsTransport` does a zero-byte read before each real read, so the zero-byte read now consumes the pending result and the real read waits for the next frame, dropping data. Move the `_receiveTcs = new(...)` line back below the zero-byte check, so a zero-byte read only waits for data and the following real read consumes it and resets the TCS.

findings.title: Unrelated test edits ride along on an automated dependency PR
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs` line 362, restore `internal sealed class WebSocketWrapper`. Nothing subclasses it, and the repo convention (CA1852) is to seal internal types. Also consider moving the non-dependency test changes in this file and in `WebSocketCompressionTests.cs` into a separate PR from the Arcade bump.

findings.title: eng/common sync matches upstream Arcade and hardens LocateVisualStudio
findings.body:
The vendored script changes are good:

- Every `Invoke-WebRequest` gets `-UseBasicParsing`, which avoids the IE-engine dependency on Windows PowerShell 5.1.
- `LocateVisualStudio` now checks that `tools.vs` and its `version`/`components` exist before reading them, so a `global.json` without a `vs` section no longer errors.
- The source-index default of main-only is harmless here, because `.azure/pipelines/ci.yml` already enables source indexing only on `refs/heads/main`.

::code{file="eng/common/tools.ps1" lines="550-573"}
